rulings.evidence: quinoa-uncooked is a LIVE board id (2 of 7 stores, cheapest 0.1372 at Sam's Club), so this is a REUSE and not a new id. The missing piece is a vocabulary ROW for the name, which is a naming question, not a registrar one.

rulings.raw: 3 Cups Cooked Chicken – skin discarded if applicable; chicken shredded or chopped
rulings.evidence: The pre-resolver flagged rotisserie-chicken as DIFFERENT FORM 'cooked', but rotisserie chicken is SOLD cooked and this line calls for cooked shredded meat with skin discarded: same form, same price class. Mapping to raw chicken-breast or thigh would be the real form flip (raw price, and a 30% cook loss on the gram weight).

rulings.raw: 1 (4.5 ounce) Can Chopped Green Chiles – drained
rulings.evidence: The 'DIFFERENT FORM: canned' flag is spurious here - the recipe line IS a can ('1 (4.5 ounce) Can'). Chopped and diced green chiles are the same product; board carries it 6 of 7 stores.

rulings.raw: ¾ Cup Roasted Corn Kernels – canned or frozen (drained if using canned)
rulings.evidence: Board ABSENT for this phrase, but a corn commodity very likely exists under another spelling (frozen-corn, canned-corn, sweet-corn) and I cannot verify the four namespaces from the table, so I refuse to propose a new id. Null gives safe pantry-static pricing while the term is hunted.

rulings.raw: ¾ Cup Black Beans – drained and rinsed
rulings.evidence: 'Drained and rinsed' is canned usage, not dry beans, so the canned row is the same form and not a flip; board carries canned-black-beans 7 of 7 stores. Seasoned Black Beans is a different seasoned product.

rulings.raw: 1 tsp EACH: Garlic Powder, Cumin, and Chili Powder
rulings.term: garlic powder, cumin, and chili powder
rulings.canon_item: Garlic Powder, Cumin, and Chili Powder
rulings.evidence: Three separate pantry spices on one unsplittable line, so no single bid can carry it; the board's 'garlic' match is fresh bulb garlic, a different food, price class and gram weight from garlic powder. Null is pantry-static and safe at 8 g total.

rulings.raw: 1 ½ Cups Colby Jack, Monterey Jack OR Pepper Jack Cheese – freshly shredded, divided
rulings.term: colby jack, monterey jack or pepper jack cheese
rulings.evidence: Monterey Jack is the middle option the source names and a same-form vocabulary row; I chose the named variety over the board's generic shredded-cheese because blend pricing is a different price class (the red-onion-is-not-onions precedent).
